title: Kernel Latency Sheriff: per-arch & seqlen guardrails for kernel selection
creator: Marcus Liu
description:
Problem: Our runtime picks kernels based on static cost heuristics which miss interactions between GPU architecture, sequence-length distribution, and prefill vs decode phases. Result: tail latency regressions for certain customer workloads (conversational bursts with long prefill + short decode) and suboptimal GPU utilization.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, runtime-enforced "Sheriff" layer that monitors per-kernel latency behavior across arch + seqlen slices and enforces guardrail decisions (preferred kernel, soft fallback, emergency demotion) while feeding data into an offline autotuner. The Sheriff must have minimal overhead, be safe by default, and allow controlled rollouts.

Approach summary:
1) Scoring model: compute a composite score for each candidate kernel per request: score = baseline_cost + arch_penalty + seqlen_multiplier + tail_risk_penalty + stability_bonus. Baseline_cost is the existing microbenchmark estimate; arch_penalty and seqlen_multiplier are small additive offsets derived from a lightweight lookup table; tail_risk_penalty increases for kernels with volatile 95/99p observed latencies; stability_bonus rewards kernels with consistent latencies across recent samples.
2) Probe fabric: continuous micro-probes (controlled sample budget ~0.5% of requests) run short, representative prefills/decodes across kernel candidates to capture 50/95/99p latency and GPU occupancy. Probes are randomized across nodes and seeded by traffic fingerprint to avoid correlated bias.
3) Safety policies: threshold-based demotion rules (e.g., if 99p rises > 2x baseline and absolute 99p > SLA-guard, immediately demote to fallback kernel for that tenant/model for N minutes) and conservative warmstart (prefer previously stable kernel when work switches from prefill to decode).
4) Autotune feedback loop: periodic offline tuner (nightly) ingests probe and production telemetry to update arch/seqlen penalty tables and candidate kernel ranking. Tuner uses a constrained optimizer (objective = minimize expected token-latency subject to cost delta <= 5%) and emits recommended policy patches.
5) Rollout plan: feature gated with per-tenant opt-in, canary on internal load, staged increase in probe budget, and monitor cost/latency delta.

Why different from prior work: existing autotuners focus on bulk cost surfaces or bandit exploration; Sheriff is a runtime guardrail that prioritizes SLA-preserving choices and feeds a separate constrained autotuner. Emphasis on tiny probe budget, per-tenant emergency demotion, and distinguish between prefill vs decode phases for kernel preference.

Success metrics (benchmarks):
- Reduce observed 99p latency regressions on internal conversational benchmark by >= 15% vs baseline when enabled.
- No more than 3% cost increase in canary; target cost neutral after autotuner updates.
- Automatic demotion should avoid customer-visible errors (rollbacks <1 per week in canary).

Links: Design doc (internal): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aSheriffDesign
Implementation PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4587
Investigation dashboard (datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/sheriff-probes/latency-overview
acceptance_criteria: Sheriff can compute per-request kernel score with <0.5ms median overhead in canary cluster
Probe fabric collects meaningful 50/95/99p metrics across kernels and arch slices with configured budget
Safety policy triggers demotion and fallback within 2s of threshold breach and records audit event
Offline tuner consumes probe + prod telemetry and emits updated penalty tables that improve 99p on validation sets
Feature rollouts, canary, and tenant opt-in controls are wired in console and documented
comments: 2026-02-22 Marcus Liu: Kickoff meeting notes: scoped minimal viable Sheriff (score + probe fabric + emergency demote). Agreed to keep probe budget <=0.5% for canary. Action: Priya to draft probe sampling policy.

2026-02-27 Priya Desai: Initial scoring prototype implemented in branch eng/sheriff/scoring. Microbench results on A100 show 0.42ms added median latency for scoring path. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4587

2026-03-02 Data team: Early probe runs (canary cluster) show interesting divergence: for seqlen>1024 on Ampere V1, kernel-k3 99p is 2.3x baseline while mean is similar. We'll add a stability bonus to penalize high-variance kernels.

2026-03-04 Performance engineering review (Jonah Kim): Concern about probe bias — recommend stratified sampling by tenant and avoiding probes during heavy GC windows. Action: add jitter to probe schedule and exclude known noisy intervals.
2026-03-08 Priya Desai: Implemented emergency demotion audit event and console toggle. Per-tenant opt-in UI mock: https://figma.com/file/sheriff-ui. Need PM and design review before canary expansion.

2026-03-10 Marcus Liu: Canary run (24h) summary: 99p reduced 18% on conversational benchmark; probe budget 0.45%; cost delta +1.2% primarily from rare conservative demotions. Decision: advance to 3-node canary for 72h, then trigger nightly tuner run. Logged follow-up ENG tasks for visibility hooks and long-term storage of probe traces.
